slide1.headline: EU AI Act: Deployer Evidence Gaps
slide1.subtitle: SMEs may miss deadlines

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: The EU AI Act has identified evidence gaps that deployers must address before 2 August 2026.
Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) may struggle to meet these deadlines.
The Act requires deployers to provide evidence of their AI systems' compliance with EU regulations.
The evidence gaps include the lack of transparency and explainability in AI decision-making.

slide3.title: INSIGHTS
bullets: The EU AI Act aims to ensure the safe and responsible development of AI systems.
SMEs may need to invest in new technologies and processes to comply with the Act.
The deadline for compliance is 2 August 2026, which may be challenging for some SMEs to meet.

slide1.subtitle: Vetted researchers can access the AI model

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: OpenAI has opened GPT-5.5-Cyber to vetted security researchers.
The AI model is designed to help security teams identify and respond to cyber threats.
The model has been trained on a large dataset of cyber security-related text.
The goal is to improve the effectiveness of security teams in detecting and responding to cyber attacks.

The use of AI in cyber security has the potential to revolutionize the field.
